extraction.name: Video-MME
extraction.description: The first-ever comprehensive Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark of MLLMs in video analysis, consisting of 900 videos across 6 visual domains and 30 fine-grained categories, with 2,700 high-quality multiple-choice question-answer pairs (3 per video), and associated subtitles and audio for multimodal evaluation.
extraction.creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
extraction.citeAs: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun. Video-MME: The First-Ever Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark of Multi-modal LLMs in Video Analysis. arXiv:2405.21075v3, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The construction of the Video-MME dataset involves three main steps: video collection, question-answer annotation, and quality review. The authors established a domain hierarchy for sourcing raw videos from YouTube, identifying 6 key domains and 30 finely-grained video categories. For each category, they collected short (<2 minutes), medium (4-15 minutes), and long (30-60 minutes) videos, and also obtained corresponding meta-information such as subtitles (if provided) and audios. The resulting dataset consists of 900 videos, including 744 videos with subtitles and all 900 with audios.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper states that the dataset consists of 900 videos, including 744 videos with subtitles and all 900 with audios. Subtitles were collected if provided.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw videos were sourced from YouTube. Corresponding meta-information such as subtitles (if provided) and audios were also obtained.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors established a domain hierarchy with 6 key domains and 30 finely-grained categories, collected videos across short, medium, and long durations, and filtered out QA pairs that could be answered solely based on textual questions by providing text-only questions to Gemini 1.5 Pro. Questions that did not meet this criterion were returned to the original annotator for revision.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For evaluation, frames were extracted from videos. For Gemini 1.5 Pro, frames were sampled at 1 frame per second for short and medium videos, and at 1 frame every 2 seconds for long videos to ensure API stability. For other models, frame extraction followed official guidelines with a fixed number of uniformly sampled frames. In the subtitle-enabled setting, subtitles corresponding to the timestamps of the sampled video frames were selected to ensure synchronization between visual and textual inputs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: After collecting raw video data, the authors annotated the videos with high-quality multiple-choice QA pairs. They recruited annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning. Each annotator thoroughly viewed the entire video and iteratively created three relevant questions, each with four candidate options, for a total of 2,700 QA pairs. Questions encompassed 12 distinct task types including perception, reasoning, and information synthesis. Each QA pair then underwent examination by a different annotator to verify clarity, answerability, logical consistency of options, and appropriateness of the designated correct answer. To ensure questions required video content, text-only questions were given to Gemini 1.5 Pro and QA pairs answerable from text alone were filtered out and returned for revision.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each QA pair was reviewed by a different annotator for clarity, answerability, logical consistency, and correctness of the designated answer. To ensure questions required video content as a critical clue, the authors provided text-only questions to Gemini 1.5 Pro and filtered out QA pairs that could be answered solely from the textual questions. Questions failing this criterion were returned to the original annotator for revision. Statistical analysis showed Gemini 1.5 Pro achieved less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators were recruited with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and findings underscore the need for further improvements in handling longer sequences and multimodal data, shedding light on future MLLM development. The authors expect that the benchmark, evaluation findings, detailed analysis, and outlined insights will inspire future progress toward more capable and robust MLLMs.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper states that the options (A/B/C/D) follow a near-uniform distribution (25.1/27.2/25.3/22.4%), ensuring an unbiased evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that subtitles are available for only 744 of 900 videos. It also discusses that long videos exhibit a long-tailed distribution with fewer samples as duration increases. The authors note that as video duration increases, model performance declines due to increased proportion of difficult reasoning tasks, increased sparsity in frame sampling for many models, and increased difficulty in long-context understanding. They also note that most open-source models do not support audio input, so audio evaluation is omitted for them.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed as a benchmark to evaluate multimodal large language models on video understanding tasks. It is used for assessing model performance across short, medium, and long videos, and across multimodal input settings including frames only, frames with subtitles, and frames with audio. The benchmark is applicable to both image and video MLLMs.
